Senses.Explanation: The ground of the actual. Yuanwu Keqin builds his hall address on it — one is all: the ground of the actual; all is one: originally no thing — picking it up dry and crackling, setting it down dense and continuous, standing alone through the three realms with nowhere in the ten directions to lodge the body; Dahui Zonggao, in his anthology voice, mocks the crowd's grading of two worthies as one-gets-body one-gets-use as dwarfs watching a play, then states the tag — not one dust received, not one dharma abandoned — I am king of the dharma, at ease in it, now repressing, now raising, nothing gained or lost; and Zhongfeng Mingben answers a trainee beset by dullness and distraction that these in their whole being are local scenery — in the ground of the actual there is no second dharma. Wuyi Yuanlai confesses at the entry-dialogue seat that in thirty years the ground has stood pierced and unobstructed for him, yet in the measure of affairs much still contradicts the principle; Sanshan Denglai raises the old Lumen exchange — asked the ground, Lumen answered the southern continent and the northern, the monk cried one family, Lumen set a Sumeru between — then answers for himself: were someone to ask Gaofeng, he would say only the Kaixi temple on the peak; Linquan Conglun reads a verse's image as the empty kalpa before Glorious Voice, like the buddha before appearing — no dharma to speak, no being to save, the ground receiving not one dust — until dawn lays out the thirty-two marks and the twelvefold teaching line by line; Liao'an Qingyu carves it into his white-cloud hermitage inscription — the blue of mountains, the white of clouds, the ground receiving not one dust, and mountains and clouds themselves wheel-spun illusions; and Poshan Haiming closes his summer-release address on it, then asks whether Deshan's stick, Linji's shout, hemp-three-pound and dried-shit-brush can still serve as ghost-and-spirit tea-rice and full-measure fodder.

Senses.Explanation: ‘On the ground of the real, not a speck is admitted’ clears away any fixed object to hold there. Masters often pair it with a line about leaving no act undone, then ask how a person can work in the world without lodging in either half. Ruibai Mingxue uses the line to address Devadatta as both the Buddha's enemy and a future Buddha. Yinyuan Longqi pairs it with omitting no work, then names the roles needed to build and run a monastery. Yunwai Xingze says the real ground receives no speck while the gate of action lacks nothing. At a funeral fire Zixian Jue gives the line, then insists that something remains to be met in the sea of birth and death. Linquan Conglun invokes the no-speck ground after an old shovel case and asks how it can coexist with active response. Dahui Zonggao rejects a tidy reading that splits the pair into pure essence and worldly use.

Senses.Explanation: The transient-guest quarters are the monastery's office and lodging for newly arrived or short-stay monks, supplied with beds and provisions and governed by arrival rules. Other regulations direct a transient guest to ask where the quarters are, unload there, and meet the guest prefect. Lamp biographies use the same institution in arrival narratives: monks meet or fight there, and the rules for new arrivals determine whether they remain. Senses.Explanation: Broken tiles and rubble (瓦礫) are discarded fragments of roof tile and masonry. The records use the literal debris in comparisons—“recognizing objects as seeing” is likened to holding rubble, and the question “rubble has no mind; should it also be the Way?” tests an inference from (無心). Public addresses also pair rubble with walls, light, radiance, or gold: “When released, rubble shines; when held fast, gold loses its colour” (放行也瓦礫生煇，把住也黃金失色) explicitly contrasts shining rubble with gold losing colour. The concrete material remains the referent in both literal and evaluative uses.

Senses.Explanation: The Mirror of Qin is a named mirror repeatedly brought into Chan verse and exchange as an instrument before which a form, a speaking participant, or the person himself is exposed and distinguished. In the Recorded Sayings of Master Baiyu, Baiyu Jingsi says that before the mirror a jackal has no way to hide its original form; in the Recorded Sayings of Konggu Daocheng, Konggu Daocheng hangs the mirror at the head of a staff and says that every dust-mote land becomes responsive. In direct questioning recorded in the Recorded Sayings of Master Hansong, Hansong Zhicao answers after the absence of the mirror prompts the question how one can distinguish the matter. The compilers Jing and Yun, narrating Xuefeng Yicun's biography in the Zutang Collection, place Xuefeng face-to-face with the mirror and tell him to inspect himself. These are observable uses of the mirror in appraisal and exposure, not a claim that every mention carries one secret fixed meaning. The headword is repeatedly attested in the corpus.

ClaimAnchors.Kwic: 且道分個甚麼？盤江河木橋原秪用幾條鐵鍊，關嶺馬跑井廟神乃是漢關將軍，來往客人古今祈禱不盡，於中求長壽得長壽、求富饒得富饒、求官位得官位、求安穩得安穩，失然有不得意者，返怪神明籤不靈，看來總是不知恩。」遂拍手呵呵大笑，云：「還知麼？松巋恁麼告報孟八郎漢，又切莫錯認定盤星。」喝一喝，下坐。上堂。「一二三四五六七，獻寶波斯樹上立；七六五四三二一，碧眼胡僧覷不及。付與東村王大老，笑倒西村石土地，惹得胡張三、黑李四，二人冷地不甘，直得眉毛廝結、兩腳捎空，走到松巋峰頂，揚聲大叫曰：『長老！不是，不是。』山僧自恃徉不睬，拄杖子忍俊不禁，輕輕𨁝跳出來，當頭一拶，二人只得冰消瓦解，疾走無邊。然後拄杖子款款地道：『也大奇，也大奇，灼然有理不相欺。不然，總是錯認定盤星，那能識得鉤頭意？』且道：如何是鉤頭意？」卓拄杖，云：「南山起雲，北山下雨。」上堂。「若論者個事，一一有來源。甚麼來源？天乾一定是荒年，水旱也亦然，直得晴雨兩相稱，恰好是豐年。所以道：『苦瓜連根苦，甜瓜徹蒂甜。』還會麼？」擊拂子，云：「穿破綾纙只是衣，喫盡千般莫過鹽，滋味本無別，何用假言傳？咦！不言傳，將謂壺中別有天。」上堂。「平施大用沒多般，一句當陽仔細看，直下了明無漸次，回頭鐵馬更加鞭。大眾！既是直下了明無漸次，因甚麼回頭鐵馬又更加鞭？」良久，云：「棒打石人頭血出，知音定不等閒看。」本師善權和尚忌。拈香云：「觸不得，背不得，橫按莫邪活捉賊；觸也得，背也得，直下證龜翻成鱉。松巋不是揚家醜，分明有話當人說。且道說個甚麼？今日先師忌辰，設供上香禮拜。」上堂。「千千有個頭，萬萬有個尾。有頭有尾，花開碓嘴；無頭無尾，是何神鬼？三世諸佛弄鬼、歷代祖師弄鬼、古今天下老和尚弄鬼，盡十方湖海衲子總在鬼窟裏作活計。松巋今日路見不平，且要向鬼神莫測處施大機、顯大用，與諸人通個消息。還委悉麼？」良久云：「又添得一個。」上堂。「直切相為，那許如何若何？但來問者，劈脊便棒，隨聲便喝。諸人若作棒喝商量，自是白雲萬里，覿面千山。直饒不作棒喝商量，亦未免驢前馬後。還委悉麼？」良久曰：「一陣風來一陣寒，冷地誰人著眼看？」幢老和尚忌。拈香云：「有利則有害，有成則有敗，三方及四維，上下並內外，不是臨濟三玄，亦非洞山五位，牛頭栴檀莫比，兜樓沉水豈賽？今日落在愚孫手裏

Senses.Explanation: The bitter half of a paired produce saying: a sweet melon is sweet through the stem, while the bitter gourd remains bitter through its root. Ying'an Tanhua speaks the line directly; Miaoyun Zhenxiong later quotes a verse attributed to Manjusri and comments on it. Wuming invokes the bitter gourd at year end; Poshan gives the image a common-root turn; Tianan speaks it in a hall sermon; Shanhui uses it as a direct answer about seeing mountains and waters.

Senses.Note: The bitter gourd is bitter down to its root; the sweet melon is sweet through its stem. The parallel tastes make a compact answer that distinguishes what is before one without adding a long theory. Tian’an folds it into a playful staff dialogue. Chaozong uses it to conclude a critique of Xiyuan’s old case. Changling gives it as a direct reply about simultaneous illumination and function. Chushi applies it to another disagreement among earlier masters, and Cishou answers a monk’s request for help with it. The bitter and sweet images gain force from those exchanges.

The origin, as raised by Yuanwu Keqin. Lingyun Zhiqin's verse on seeing the blossoms: thirty years a seeker of the sword; how many times the leaves fell and the branches sprouted again; since the one sight of peach blossoms, down to this day, no more doubt. Xuansha Shibei: proper indeed, most proper — yet I guarantee, old brother, you are not through. Says Yuanwu: a thousand-pound bow does not loose its trigger for a gnat. Lingyun had already pulled open the pivot of heaven; Xuansha then overturned the axis of earth. Tell me — which is the not-through place? Let one with the eye that passes the barrier try to discern it. Gaofeng Yuanmiao interleaves his own three-word glosses into the raising: Lingyun's awakening at the peach blossoms — a skull cracked into the glue-basin. Guishan Lingyou's word, entering by condition never to fall back — teeth clenched, sealing Yong Chi. Xuansha's word, proper indeed most proper, I guarantee the old brother is not through — tears shed, beheading Duke Ding. Clever fellow! Even if you see it right here — buy straw sandals and travel thirty more years, then come back and take Xifeng's painful staff. Even hundred-refined gold cannot escape the furnace for another smelting. Miyun Yuanwu, picking up the same case and Dahui's busied hundred households: what talk of one household's trouble and a hundred households busied — it is one blind man leading a crowd of blind. And Poshan Haiming, after the raised verse with its single-flip — from the one sight of peach blossoms, only down to today no more doubt — hears Xuansha's doubled verdict and appraises: a film in the eye, flowers falling in empty sky; had Xuansha not wielded the golden scalpel well, the man would all but have gone blind. His ode: fragrance fills the branch-tips, blossoms fill the stream; Lingyun's one sight, a clap of hands in light requital. Ha! Who knew there was still a guest in the peach orchard, not letting the spring wind slip past both eyes. Shiqi Tongyun aims the doubled verdict at the whole arsenal, at the bath-master's seat: Deshan blowing out the paper lamp at Longtan, Linji's three painful staves of Huangbo, the cypress tree in the yard, the dried shit-stick, three pounds of hemp — proper indeed, most proper, I guarantee the old brother is not through. And the four shone-uses and four selectings, guest-within-host and host-within-guest, shift upon shift, all landing free — to lift is to lift, to set is to set: what is hard in that? Only the one who cannot put down a single thread asks how the school's matter goes and how to pass through sound and sight. And Jiqi Hongchu, at the close of the Great-Compassion retreat: the Bodhisattva of what is heard advanced first in rites and music, then advanced in rites and music — grasses and trees bow their heads, earth and stone thereupon give light. But let the makara fish one morning bore through the pure precious eye, let Mount Sumeru crush down the matrix-undoing arm: thirty-two responses, fourteen fearslessnesses — proper indeed, most proper, I guarantee the old brother is not through. There is a fellow: raising his brows, fish and dragons gain their way of swimming; in a blink, ghosts and gods have no road to walk — knife-mountains broken down without Manjusri's wondrous wisdom, hells extinguished without Samantabhadra's sameness. Such is the everywhere-roundness of the way-nature, such the deep stillness of the mind-source. If today it is not verified, how will you go on afterward? Palms together: the present can be tested.

Senses.PreferredTarget: Mahakashyapa
Senses.Explanation: Kashyapa is the figure whom the Chan record places at the first public handover. At the Vulture Peak assembly, the World-Honored One holds up a flower before the silent gathering; Kashyapa alone breaks into a smile, after which the Buddha says that he entrusts the treasury of the true eye of the teaching to Mahakashyapa. Later Chan records do not leave him inside a biography: they repeatedly raise, question, and comment on this scene. Yuelin says that when the World-Honored One held up the flower and Kashyapa smiled, both deserved thirty blows. Kashyapa also appears at the teaching seat: after the assembly gathers, he strikes the sounding block and announces, “the World-Honored One has finished speaking the teaching,” and the Buddha leaves the seat. In the succession encounter with Ananda, Ananda asks what was transmitted besides the gold-thread robe; Kashyapa calls “Ananda,” receives his answer, and says, “knock down the flagpole before the gate.” These public acts—smile and announced entrustment, closing the Buddha's assembly, and the robe-and-flagpole exchange with Ananda—are Kashyapa's defining Chan deployment.
Senses.Note: This sense is Mahakashyapa, identifiable in the cited Chan cases by the flower, the entrusted eye-treasury, Ananda, or the gold-thread robe. The earlier Kashyapa Buddha is a different figure and is recorded separately below by his Zen deployment.

Senses.Explanation: Even neighboring heirs in a teaching chain do not own one another’s realization. Sanyi turns the old succession formula into a longer chain and asks whether it names absorption or a disease. Baiyu adds his own absorption to the line, then asks why the assembly still comes together at bell and board. Jifei asks how a teaching can pass if teacher and heir do not know one another’s absorption. Chunbei extends the line into a sermon on the Buddha’s awakening.
